To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

social ties, social influence, and social support are associated with lower risk of death from natural causes, and that social influence and support are associated with better physical health, less psychological distress, and better psychological well-being.

(1) social support is a multidimensional construct that includes both emotional sustenance and instrumental assistance and (2) the two types of social support have different antecedents and consequences.

(1) perceived support availability and support receipt are associated with better physical and mental health, (2) support receipt is associated with better physical health only when it involves instrumental aid, (3) support receipt is not associated with psychological well-being when the recipient has high perceived support availability, and (4) perceived support availability is a stronger predictor of physical health than is support receipt.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms through which relationships and social support influence physical and mental health.
the mechanisms through which the social environment influences the physical and emotional health of the individual.

how social ties and support affect health, how social relationships and social ties affect each other, and how social ties and social support affect health and health behaviors through their effects on the mechanisms that link social ties and support to health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

social relationships, social support, and social networks are associated with physical health, mental health, and longevity, and that these associations are mediated by the mechanisms I have discussed.

social relationships and social supports are beneficial to physical and mental health because they are a source of positive affect, self-esteem, sense, of control, purpose and meaning, and companionship, as well as a source of stress-buffering resources.
social support has been shown to be a significant predictor of physical and psychological well being, and that social support can be a significant predictor in both the direct and the indirect ways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we found that social support is a protective factor for mental health, but that the effects are not always positive and can depend on the type of support, the source of support, the recipient's characteristics, and the situation.
we have found that social relationships, and especially social support, are important for both mental and physical health, and that the effects are mediated by a variety of psychological mechanisms.

we have shown the importance of the social context in the development of health and disease, and the need to consider the role of social factors in understanding the mechanisms underlying the development of health.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the social environment is a critical determinant of health and longevity, and that the social environment can be modified to improve health outcomes.
there are two basic kinds of social support, and that the two types of social support have very different effects on physical and mental health.

social support can be conceptualized in terms of the mechanisms through which it exerts its effects on physical and mental health, and that different mechanisms may be more or less relevant depending on the nature of the stressor, the nature of the support provided, and the characteristics of the supporter and recipient.
